cultural.vision_reason: A child's reindeer-fur hooded coat with decorative triangular woolen cloth trim, a traditional garment style consistent with Yakut (and broader Siberian reindeer-herding) clothing craft.

physical.title: coat
physical.summary: A child's coat with hood, slightly flared in shape, and made from many pieces of reindeer fur.  (Also lined with fur, including hood).  Decorated with four rows of red, triangular-shaped pieces of woollen cloth, forming a panel 11 cms deep in total.  Grey fur fills the gaps between each triangle on the front; brown fur used on back.  Two vertical lines of red triangular pieces of cloth (with grey fur) stitched to upper sides, both front and back, near sleeve ends, and towards back of hood (with grey fur).  A single line is worked around the flap covering the neck and beside the hood, framing the face.  Two pieces of fur, shaped like ears, stitched to back of hood.  Mittens poking out from sleeve ends.  Coat fastened with small metal hook; thread loop missing.  Some fur has worn away, revealing cream-coloured skin beneath.
